bricks.title: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

items.why: Anterior boundary of the perineum; mons pubis overlies it

questions.q: The pubic symphysis forms which boundary of the perineum?
questions.explain: The perineum is bounded anteriorly by the pubic symphysis, laterally by the ischial tuberosities, and posteriorly by the coccyx.

items.why: Opening bounded by the superior pubic and ischiopubic rami

questions.q: Which two bony parts help bound the obturator foramen?
choices: Superior pubic ramus and ischiopubic ramus
questions.explain: The obturator foramen is bounded in part by the superior pubic ramus and the ischiopubic ramus.

items.why: Largely covers the obturator foramen

questions.q: The obturator membrane largely covers which opening?
questions.explain: The obturator foramen is largely covered by the obturator membrane.

items.why: Bounds the obturator foramen
Bounds the obturator foramen
Lateral boundary of the perineum; sacrotuberous ligament attachment

questions.q: Together with the pubic symphysis and coccyx, the ischial tuberosities form the boundaries of which region?
questions.explain: The perineum is bounded anteriorly by the pubic symphysis, laterally by the ischial tuberosities, and posteriorly by the coccyx.

items.why: Attachment of the sacrospinous ligament
Converted to the greater sciatic foramen by the ligaments

questions.q: Which ligament converts the greater sciatic notch into the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.explain: The sacrospinous (with the sacrotuberous) ligament converts the sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.

items.why: Converted to the lesser sciatic foramen

questions.q: The lesser sciatic foramen is defined by which pair of ligaments?
questions.explain: The sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments convert the lesser sciatic notch into the lesser sciatic foramen and define the boundary between the foramina.

items.why: Sacrum to ischial tuberosity

questions.q: The sacrotuberous ligament spans from the sacrum to which bony landmark?
questions.explain: The sacrotuberous ligament spans to the ischial tuberosity, while the sacrospinous ligament runs to the ischial spine.

items.why: Sacrum/coccyx to ischial spine; stabilizes sacrum

questions.q: The sacrospinous ligament extends from the sacrum and coccyx to which landmark?
questions.explain: The sacrospinous ligament extends from the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine.

questions.q: Together, the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments mainly stabilize which bone?
questions.explain: Together the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments stabilize the sacrum and define the sciatic foramina.

items.why: Posterior pelvis; uterosacral ligament attachment

questions.q: Which ligament extends from the cervix to the sacrum, supporting the uterus posteriorly?
questions.explain: The uterosacral ligament extends from the cervix to the sacrum and supports the uterus posteriorly.

items.why: Posterior boundary of the perineum

questions.q: The coccyx forms which boundary of the perineum?
questions.explain: The perineum is bounded posteriorly by the coccyx, anteriorly by the pubic symphysis, and laterally by the ischial tuberosities.

items.why: Region inferior to the pelvic diaphragm; urogenital and anal triangles

questions.q: Where does the perineum lie relative to the pelvic diaphragm?
questions.explain: The perineum is the region inferior to the pelvic diaphragm.

questions.q: The perineum is divided into which two triangles?
questions.explain: The perineum is divided into the urogenital and anal triangles, with the perineal body at their junction.

items.why: Central point at the junction of the two triangles

questions.q: Where is the perineal body located?
choices: Anterior perineum, just below the pubic symphysis
Center of the perineum, between the two triangles
Lateral perineum, beside the ischial tuberosity
Posterior perineum, at the tip of the coccyx
questions.explain: The perineal body lies centrally at the junction of the urogenital and anal triangles.

items.why: External genitalia, located in the perineum

questions.q: Which of the following is a component of the vulva?
questions.explain: The vulva consists of the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, and vestibule.

items.why: Fat pad over the pubic symphysis

questions.q: The mons pubis is a layer of fatty tissue overlying which structure?
questions.explain: The mons pubis is a layer of fatty tissue over the pubic symphysis.

items.why: Cutaneous folds, mons to perineum; round ligament ends here

questions.q: Which ligament ends in the labia majora after passing through the inguinal canal?
questions.explain: The round ligament of the uterus connects the uterine fundus to the labia majora, passing through the inguinal canal.

items.why: Smaller folds around the vaginal opening; form the clitoral hood

questions.q: The anterior junction of the labia minora forms which structure?
questions.explain: The clitoris is covered by a hood (prepuce) formed by the anterior junction of the labia minora.

items.why: Glans, body, two crura; primary erectile tissue

questions.q: Which part of the clitoris is its external portion?
questions.explain: The external portion of the clitoris is the glans; the body and crura extend beneath the vulvar tissue.

items.why: Area enclosed by the labia minora

questions.q: The area enclosed by the labia minora is called the
questions.explain: The vestibule is the area enclosed by the labia minora.

questions.q: Which openings lie within the vestibule?
questions.explain: The vestibule contains the vaginal opening (introitus), the external urethral meatus, and the vestibular glands.

items.why: Vaginal opening in the vestibule; hymen

questions.q: Which thin membrane partially surrounds the vaginal opening in most newborn females?
questions.explain: The hymen is a thin membrane that partially surrounds the vaginal opening and is present in most newborn females.

items.why: External urethral meatus in the vestibule
Mucus glands at the posterior introitus; cysts/abscesses

questions.q: Where are the greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands located?
questions.explain: Bartholin's glands sit at the posterior vaginal introitus and secrete mucus to lubricate the vulva.

questions.q: A 25-year-old has a painful swelling of the posterior labium at the vaginal opening. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explain: Bartholin's glands are most commonly associated with cysts or abscesses presenting as labial swellings that may need drainage.

items.why: Muscular canal from vulva to uterus; prolapse

questions.q: A woman with a weak pelvic floor has an anterior vaginal bulge and urinary dysfunction. Which organ has descended?
questions.explain: Loss of pelvic floor support can let the bladder descend against the anterior vagina (cystocele), causing urinary symptoms.

items.why: Connects vagina to uterus; transformation zone; effaces in labor

questions.q: Cervical dysplasia most commonly develops at which site?
questions.explain: The squamocolumnar junction (transformation zone) between ectocervix and endocervix is the most common site of cervical dysplasia and squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.q: What does the cervix do during parturition?
choices: Thickens to retain the fetus at term
Thins and effaces to let the fetus pass
Secretes fluid to lubricate the vulva
questions.explain: During childbirth the cervix thins and effaces, allowing the fetus to pass through it.

items.why: Passage from uterine cavity to vagina
Opening of the cervical canal into the uterus

questions.q: The internal os opens into which space?
questions.explain: The cervical canal opens into the uterus at the internal os and into the vagina at the external os.

items.why: Opening of the cervical canal into the vagina

questions.q: The external os opens into which space?
questions.explain: The external os is where the cervical canal opens into the vagina.

items.why: Pear-shaped organ; myometrium contracts in labor

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall contracts during labor?
questions.explain: The myometrium is mostly smooth muscle and is responsible for uterine contraction during labor.

items.why: Interstitium, isthmus, ampulla, infundibulum + fimbriae; ectopic pregnancy

questions.q: Which part of the uterine tube sweeps the ovulated oocyte into the tube?
questions.explain: The infundibulum leads to the fimbriae, which sweep the ovulated oocyte into the tube.

questions.q: A 30-year-old with left adnexal pain has a positive pregnancy test and no intrauterine sac. Where has the embryo most likely implanted?
questions.explain: The ampulla is the widest part of the tube and the usual site of fertilization, so most ectopic pregnancies occur in the tube there.

questions.q: Why is an interstitial (cornual) ectopic pregnancy especially dangerous?
choices: Myometrium lets it grow longer before rupture
The narrow lumen makes it rupture at once
It lies outside the peritoneal cavity
Its blood comes straight from the aorta
questions.explain: In the interstitial portion the surrounding myometrium allows the pregnancy to grow longer before rupture, often causing severe hemorrhage.

items.why: Gonad; ovarian vessels, para-aortic lymph, vagal parasympathetics

questions.q: Lymph from the ovary drains directly to which nodes?
questions.explain: Ovarian lymph follows the blood supply and drains directly to the para-aortic nodes, not the pelvic nodes.

questions.q: The ovary receives its parasympathetic innervation from which nerve?
questions.explain: Unlike other pelvic organs (S2-S4), the ovaries receive parasympathetic input from the vagus nerve.

items.why: Double-layered peritoneal fold over uterus, tubes, ovaries

questions.q: How is the broad ligament best described?
choices: A fibromuscular cord in the inguinal canal
A dense band from cervix to sacrum
A fascial sheath around ovarian vessels
questions.explain: The broad ligament is a double-layered peritoneal fold from the lateral pelvic walls covering the uterus, tubes, and ovaries.

items.why: Fundus to labia majora via inguinal canal

questions.q: The round ligament of the uterus passes through which passage to reach the labia majora?
questions.explain: The round ligament connects the uterine fundus to the labia majora by passing through the inguinal canal.

items.why: Ovary to lateral pelvic wall; carries ovarian vessels

questions.q: Which vessels run in the suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament of the ovary?
questions.explain: The suspensory ligament of the ovary contains the ovarian vessels and lymphatics.

questions.q: The suspensory ligament attaches the ovary to which structure?
questions.explain: The suspensory ligament attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall; the ovarian ligament attaches it to the uterus.

items.why: Pelvic diaphragm (deep layer); prolapse when weak

questions.q: The levator ani belongs to which layer of the pelvic floor?
questions.explain: The deep layer of the pelvic floor is the pelvic diaphragm: levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus) and coccygeus.

questions.q: A multiparous woman with a weak pelvic floor has a posterior vaginal bulge and difficult defecation. What has descended?
questions.explain: Loss of pelvic floor support can produce a rectocele (rectal prolapse), causing difficulty with defecation.

items.why: Completes the pelvic diaphragm

questions.q: Which muscle joins the levator ani to complete the pelvic diaphragm?
questions.explain: The pelvic diaphragm consists of the levator ani and the coccygeus.

items.why: Hip muscle forming the pelvic wall; indirect support

questions.q: How do the obturator internus and piriformis support the pelvic organs?
choices: Directly, by forming the pelvic diaphragm
By acting as a urethral sphincter
By anchoring the cervix to the sacrum
questions.explain: They are primarily hip muscles that indirectly support pelvic organs by stabilizing the pelvis, forming the 'walls' of the pelvic bowl.

items.why: Pelvic wall muscle; indirect support
Passes under the uterine artery and the suspensory ligament

questions.q: During hysterectomy, the ureter is at risk because it passes just inferior to which artery?
questions.explain: 'Water under the bridge': the ureter passes inferior to the uterine artery.

questions.q: Ligating the ovarian vessels in the suspensory ligament risks injuring which structure?
questions.explain: The ureter passes inferior and posterior to the suspensory ligament of the ovary, so it is at risk during ligation of the ovarian vessels.

items.why: Common iliac veins form the IVC; left one prone to compression

questions.q: Why is the left common iliac vein especially prone to compression?
choices: It enters the left renal vein at a right angle
It crosses rightward on a long oblique course
It runs within the broad ligament
It passes through the inguinal canal
questions.explain: The left common iliac vein must cross to the right to reach the IVC, so its longer, oblique course makes it susceptible to compression.

items.why: Anterior division supplies most female reproductive organs

questions.q: Most female reproductive organs are supplied by which division of the internal iliac artery?
questions.explain: The anterior branch of the internal iliac artery supplies most of the female reproductive organs.

questions.q: The uterine vein drains into which vein?
questions.explain: The uterine vein receives blood from the uterus and drains into the internal iliac vein.

items.why: Joins internal iliac vein to form common iliac vein
Ovarian arteries from aorta; right vein to IVC, left to left renal

questions.q: The ovarian arteries arise from which vessel?
questions.explain: The ovaries are the exception to internal iliac supply; their gonadal arteries descend from the abdominal aorta.

questions.q: The left ovarian vein drains into which vein?
questions.explain: The right ovarian vein drains directly into the IVC, while the left drains into the left renal vein.

items.why: Supplies most of the uterus; in cardinal ligament; ureter passes under

questions.q: The uterine vessels run within which ligament?
questions.explain: The cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament anchors the cervix and upper vagina to the pelvic wall and contains the uterine vessels.

questions.q: The uterine artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.explain: The uterine artery comes from the anterior branch of the internal iliac artery and supplies most of the uterus.

items.why: Dual supply of the lower uterine segment

questions.q: The lower uterine segment has a dual supply from the uterine artery and branches of which artery?
questions.explain: The lower uterine segment has a dual blood supply that includes branches of the vaginal artery.

items.why: Sensory to inferior vagina/external genitalia; motor to pelvic floor

questions.q: Which nerve gives motor supply to the pelvic floor and sensation to the inferior vagina?
questions.explain: The pudendal nerve provides sensory innervation to the inferior vagina/external genitalia and motor innervation to the pelvic floor muscles.

bricks.title: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

items.why: Gonads: spermatogenesis and testosterone; aortic supply, para-aortic nodes

questions.q: Testicular cancer usually metastasizes first to which lymph nodes?
questions.explain: Testicular lymph follows the gonadal arteries to the para-aortic nodes, the most common site of initial metastasis.

questions.q: Sympathetic innervation of the testes arises from which spinal levels?
questions.explain: Testicular sympathetics come from T10-T11; the other pelvic organs get sympathetics from L1-L2.

questions.q: Parasympathetic innervation of the testes comes from which nerve?
questions.explain: The testes receive parasympathetic innervation from the vagus nerve, unlike other pelvic organs (S2-S4).

items.why: Sac of smooth muscle and skin holding the testes; inguinal lymph

questions.q: Lymph from the scrotum drains to which nodes?
questions.explain: Although near the testes, the scrotum drains to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.

items.why: Posterior to testis; sperm storage and maturation; epididymitis

questions.q: What is the main function of the epididymis?
questions.explain: The epididymis is a long convoluted tube posterior to the testis responsible for storage and maturation of sperm.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active man has epididymitis. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: Epididymitis is commonly caused by gonococcus in young males and by E. coli in older males.

items.why: Vas deferens, vessels, nerves; three fascial coverings

questions.q: Which layers wrap the spermatic cord, from outer to inner?
questions.explain: The spermatic cord is wrapped by external spermatic fascia, cremasteric muscle, and internal spermatic fascia.

questions.q: Which of the following runs within the spermatic cord?
questions.explain: The spermatic cord contains the vas deferens, blood and lymphatic vessels (including the pampiniform plexus), and nerves.

items.why: Carries sperm; sympathetic peristalsis; vasectomy

questions.q: After a vasectomy, which component is absent from the ejaculate?
questions.explain: Vasectomy severs the vas deferens, blocking sperm transport; seminal vesicle and prostate secretions still form the ejaculate.

items.why: Fructose-rich fluid, 70-85% of seminal volume; semenogelin

questions.q: Seminal vesicle secretion is especially rich in which sugar?
questions.explain: Seminal vesicle fluid has a high fructose concentration, providing energy for sperm.

questions.q: About how much of the seminal fluid volume comes from the seminal vesicles?
questions.explain: The seminal vesicles contribute roughly 70%-85% of seminal fluid volume; the prostate adds about a third.

items.why: Vas deferens + seminal vesicle duct; open into prostatic urethra

questions.q: Each ejaculatory duct is formed by the vas deferens joining which duct?
questions.explain: Excretory ducts of the seminal vesicles merge with the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory ducts.

items.why: Between bladder and rectum; alkaline fluid; zones; vertebral spread

questions.q: Which prostatic zone, though small, causes most symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia?
questions.explain: The transitional zone is only ~5% of volume, but its enlargement compresses the prostatic urethra and causes most BPH symptoms.

questions.q: The prostate is supplied primarily by which artery?
questions.explain: The prostate receives blood mainly from the inferior vesical artery, a branch of the internal iliac.

questions.q: Prostate cancer spreads to the vertebrae through a connection with which venous network?
questions.explain: The prostatic plexus drains to the internal iliac vein, which connects with the vertebral venous plexus, a route for vertebral metastasis.

items.why: Urethra within the prostate; ejaculatory ducts open here

questions.q: Which ducts open into the prostatic urethra?
questions.explain: Within the prostate the two ejaculatory ducts join the prostatic urethra, where seminal and prostatic secretions mix.

items.why: Short segment distal to the prostate
Penile urethra in corpus spongiosum; lubricated by bulbourethral fluid

questions.q: What does bulbourethral (Cowper) gland fluid do in the spongy urethra?
choices: Forms a third of the semen
questions.explain: Bulbourethral glands secrete a clear pre-ejaculate that lubricates the distal urethra and neutralizes its acidic pH.

items.why: Glans and body; supply from internal pudendal arteries

questions.q: Penile arterial supply comes mainly from branches of which artery?
questions.explain: The major blood supply of the penis comes from the internal iliac via the internal pudendal arteries.

items.why: Paired dorsal erectile bodies; deep arteries; parasympathetic erection

questions.q: Erection results from which autonomic action?
questions.explain: Parasympathetic nerves dilate penile blood vessels to produce erection ('point'); sympathetic nerves constrict and inhibit.

questions.q: Which arteries supply the erectile tissue of the corpora cavernosa?
questions.explain: Internal pudendal branches include the deep penile (cavernosal) arteries to the erectile tissue and dorsal arteries to skin, glans, and fascia.

items.why: Single ventral erectile body surrounding the urethra

questions.q: The corpus spongiosum surrounds which structure?
questions.explain: The single ventral corpus spongiosum surrounds and protects the spongy (penile) urethra.

items.why: Supplies pelvic viscera; begins at L5-S1

questions.q: At what vertebral level does the internal iliac artery begin?
questions.explain: The internal iliac artery begins at the level of the L5-S1 intervertebral disc; its anterior branches supply the reproductive viscera.

items.why: Testicular arteries from aorta; left vein to left renal vein

questions.q: The testicular arteries originate from which vessel?
questions.explain: Unlike other reproductive arteries, the testicular (gonadal) arteries branch directly off the abdominal aorta.

questions.q: The left testicular vein drains into which vein?
questions.explain: The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein; the right drains directly into the IVC.

items.why: Gives the deep and dorsal arteries of the penis

questions.q: Which branches of the internal pudendal artery supply the penis?
questions.explain: The internal pudendal arteries branch into the deep penile (cavernosal) arteries and the dorsal arteries.

items.why: Supplies skin, glans, fascia

questions.q: What does the dorsal artery of the penis supply?
questions.explain: Dorsal arteries supply the skin, glans, and fascia; deep (cavernosal) arteries supply the erectile tissue.

items.why: Drains the penis
Testicular venous network in the cord; varicocele

questions.q: Why is a varicocele of the pampiniform plexus more common on the left?
choices: Left vein enters the renal vein at a right angle
Left vein drains straight into the IVC
Left testicular artery comes from the renal
Left plexus lies outside the spermatic cord
questions.explain: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a right angle, raising venous pressure and causing 'bag of worms' dilation.

questions.q: The right pampiniform plexus drains via the right gonadal vein into which vessel?
questions.explain: The right pampiniform plexus drains via the right gonadal vein directly into the IVC.

items.why: Somatic motor and sensory supply of the perineum (S2-S4)

questions.q: The pudendal nerve arises from which spinal levels?
questions.explain: The primary somatic motor and sensory innervation of the pelvic and perineal structures comes from the pudendal nerve (S2-S4).

bricks.title: Structure and Function of the Breast

items.why: Breast lies on pectoralis major; retromammary space; 2nd-6th rib base

questions.q: The breast sits directly on which muscle?
questions.explain: The breasts sit in front of the pectoralis major on the chest wall.

questions.q: The retromammary space lies between which two layers?
choices: Deep superficial fascia and pectoral fascia
questions.explain: The retromammary space, mostly loose connective tissue, lies between the deep layer of the superficial fascia and the pectoral fascia.

questions.q: The base of the breast spans vertically between which ribs?
questions.explain: The circular base of the breast spans vertically from the second rib to the sixth rib.

items.why: Landmark defining axillary node levels I-III

questions.q: Level II axillary nodes lie in what position relative to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explain: Axillary levels are defined by the pectoralis minor: Level I lateral, Level II posterior, Level III medial.

questions.q: Axillary nodes medial to the pectoralis minor are classified as
questions.explain: Level III axillary nodes lie medial to the pectoralis minor.

items.why: Gives the internal thoracic artery

questions.q: The internal thoracic artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.explain: The internal thoracic artery, a main breast supply, branches from the subclavian artery.

items.why: Major medial breast supply

questions.q: Which two arteries are the primary blood supply of the breast?
questions.explain: The breast is supplied primarily by the internal thoracic (from subclavian) and lateral thoracic (from axillary) arteries.

items.why: Gives the lateral thoracic artery

questions.q: The lateral thoracic artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.explain: The lateral thoracic artery, a main breast supply, branches from the axillary artery.

items.why: Major lateral breast supply

questions.q: Besides the internal and lateral thoracic arteries, which arteries add blood to the breast?
questions.explain: Additional breast supply comes from the thoracoacromial artery and the posterior intercostal arteries.

items.why: Main venous drainage of the breast

questions.q: Venous drainage of the breast occurs predominantly through which veins?
questions.explain: Breast venous drainage is predominantly through the lateral thoracic veins (to the axillary veins) and internal thoracic veins.

items.why: Receives the lateral thoracic veins

questions.q: The lateral thoracic veins of the breast empty into which vein?
questions.explain: Breast venous blood returns largely via the lateral thoracic veins to the axillary veins.

items.why: Papilla at the areola center; lactiferous ducts and sinuses open here

questions.q: What is the correct path of milk to the nipple?
questions.explain: Milk is produced in alveoli, travels through lactiferous ducts, then dilated lactiferous sinuses to reach the nipple.

questions.q: The nipple is also known as the
questions.explain: The lactiferous sinuses connect to the nipple, also known as the papilla.

items.why: Surrounds the nipple
